title: CICAN Dublin Archive — Batch 066 candidate evidence packet

candidates.official_title: John McElhinney & Co., 7 Seville Place, Dublin 1, DUBLIN
candidates.description_summary: Terraced two-bay two-storey house over raised basement, now in office use. M-profile slate roof hipped to the south behind parapet with granite coping; yellow Flemish-bond brick walls with rusticated granite quoins at the north end; granite plinth over rendered basement; gauged-brick window openings and replacement six-over-six timber sash windows. Round-headed entrance with moulded render surround and Doric doorcase; original flat-panelled timber door, engaged Doric columns, panelled lintel cornice and replacement petal fanlight. Shared granite platform and ten granite steps with intermediate platform; decorative cast-iron railings.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH identifies this as a mid-sized early Victorian former townhouse in a terrace of seven similar houses on the west side of Seville Place. It retains its original doorcase and ironmongery and contributes to the residential streetscape.

candidates.description_summary: End-of-terrace two-bay two-storey house over raised basement. M-profile slate roof behind parapet; yellow Flemish-bond brick walls with rusticated granite quoins at the north corner; granite plinth over rendered basement; gauged-brick window openings and early replacement two-over-two timber sash windows. candidates.description_summary: End-of-terrace two-bay three-storey house over raised basement, one of a group of five similar houses. M-profile slate roof hipped to the north behind parapet with granite coping; red Flemish-bond brick walls on granite plinth over rendered basement; gauged-brick window openings and early replacement two-over-two timber sliding sash windows to ground and first floors, three-over-three to second floor, with earlier timber sash windows to rear. Round-headed entrance with moulded surround and Doric doorcase; original eleven-panel timber door, engaged Doric columns and plain glazed fanlight. Extended granite platform shared with the neighbour to the north, with cast-iron bootscraper and coal-hole cover.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH identifies this as an important component of a terrace of seven tall red-brick houses dating from the late Georgian period. It retains an early doorcase, door, some good fenestration and overall composition.
